one_line: Misldar and leader of the Dal Khalsa who led Sikh resistance during the Vadda Ghallughara of 1762.

appearance.age_look: mid-40s, broad-shouldered, sturdy and battle-hardened with disciplined posture
appearance.face: oval face with a strong jaw, wheatish Punjabi complexion, high straight nose, thick brows, short well-kept black beard slightly streaked with grey, deep-set determined eyes with a calm yet intense gaze, default expression a steady composed focus that hints at protective resolve
appearance.hair: long black hair tied in a tight topknot (joora) fully covered by a deep navy-blue tall domed dastar wrapped neatly with a slightly pointed crown and a simple steel khanda-style ornament at the front, no plume or excess decoration
appearance.costume: era-accurate mid-18th century Sikh warrior attire: a knee-length deep navy-blue woolen chola (tunic) with slightly flared skirt and side slits for riding, worn over a lighter indigo cotton kameez and matching churidar-style trousers; over this a fitted quilted dark indigo angarkha-style overcoat suggesting concealed padding, fastened with cloth ties; a broad matte steel kara on his right wrist and a couple of thinner karas on the left; around his waist a wide mustard-ochre cotton kamarband wrapped several times, from which smaller sheathed kirpans and pouches hang; on his feet sturdy brown leather jutti with upturned toes, dust-worn; across his torso a simple dark brown leather cross-belt holding a powder horn and small pouch, with minimal metal decoration suited to a constantly moving warrior rather than a court noble
appearance.signature: a single slightly curved Sikh-talwar with a plain steel hilt and disc pommel, carried sheathed in a brown leather scabbard with subtle brass fittings and usually held in his left hand or resting against his shoulder as he shields the non-combatants behind him

ref_desc: Jassa Singh Ahluwalia is a mid-40s broad-shouldered Sikh leader with wheatish complexion, short black-and-grey beard, navy-blue domed dastar, deep navy chola over indigo garments, mustard-ochre kamarband, brown leather belts and jutti, and a plain steel-hilted talwar in a brown scabbard.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of Jassa Singh Ahluwalia: a mid-40s broad-shouldered Punjabi Sikh leader with an oval face, wheatish complexion, strong jaw, high nose, thick brows and a short well-kept black beard lightly streaked with grey, his default expression calm and resolute as he protects others. His long hair is tied in a joora fully covered by a deep navy-blue tall domed dastar wrapped neatly, with a simple steel khanda-style ornament at the front and no plume. He wears a knee-length deep navy-blue woolen chola with a slightly flared skirt and side slits over a lighter indigo cotton kameez and matching churidar trousers, topped by a fitted quilted dark indigo angarkha-style overcoat fastened with cloth ties that hints at hidden padding. Around his waist is a wide mustard-ochre cotton kamarband holding small sheathed kirpans and pouches, and across his chest a plain dark brown leather cross-belt with a powder horn and small pouch, all practical and minimally decorated. His wrists show a broad matte steel kara on the right and thinner karas on the left, and he wears worn brown leather jutti with upturned toes. His signature weapon is a single slightly curved Sikh talwar with a plain steel hilt and disc pommel in a brown leather scabbard with subtle brass fittings, held in his left hand or resting against his shoulder. Use a palette dominated by deep navy blue, indigo, mustard ochre, brown leather and matte steel grey, and present front, side and back views to clearly show his face, hair, garments, and weapon consistently.
